dropped.item: The talk will 'draw on that experience' (his 15 years of research). The explicit link between his background and the talk's content is gone.
'the questions facing those responsible for peatland resilience'. The framing of open questions is collapsed into 'what wildfire demands of the people'.

changed.item: 'what the 2025 season means' became 'what last year's fires mean'. An explicit year is replaced by a relative reference. This assumes the summit takes place in 2026, which the original never states, and would be wrong or confusing if the text is read at another time.

'His work provides a long-term perspective on the challenges posed by wildfire' became 'That long view gives him a clear sense of what wildfire demands'. The subject shifts from his work offering a perspective to others, to him personally having a 'clear sense', which is a stronger claim of certainty.
'the 2025 season' became 'fires'. The scope narrows from a whole fire season (which could include conditions, absence of fires, or policy response) to the fires themselves.
'how research can inform the decisions that follow' became 'how research can help shape what happens next'. Decision-making by people is generalised to outcomes in general.

added.item: The implied claim that the 2025 fire season was 'last year' relative to the summit or the reader.
The characterisation that he has a 'clear sense' of what wildfire demands, a mildly stronger assertion of authority.
